1.title: Modules: Scope, Inputs, Outputs and Composition
1.text: Welcome to Module twelve: Modules: Scope, Inputs, Outputs and Composition. It covers the exam area five. Terraform modules. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do three things. five B Describe variable scope within modules. five C Use modules in configuration. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: five. Terraform modules. Exam format: a one-hour online-proctored multiple-choice exam on Terraform one point one two. Validated against: the official Terraform Associate version oh oh four exam objectives.

1.title: Scope: modules are isolated
1.text: Scope: modules are isolated. A module is its own scope. Its variables, locals and resources are private to it. The only ways data crosses the boundary are.

1.title: Scope: modules are isolated, continued
1.text: Scope: modules are isolated. The figure shows this: Inputs flow into a module and outputs flow back; nothing else crosses.

1.title: Scope: modules are isolated, continued
1.text: Scope: modules are isolated. Parent to child. Input variables: arguments in the module block. Child to parent. Output values: read as module dot N A M E dot O U T P U T. The parent cannot read a child's resources, locals or variables directly, and the child cannot read the parent's.

1.title: Scope: modules are isolated, continued
1.text: Scope: modules are isolated. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study. Exam tip: A module only sees what is passed in as variables, and the parent only sees what the module exposes as outputs. Reference a child output as module dot N A M E dot O U T P U T N A M E.

1.title: Using a module in configuration
1.text: Using a module in configuration. Call it. A module name block with source. Pass inputs. Arguments that match the module's variables; required variables must be set. Run terraform init. Download the module (and re-run after adding or changing it). Use outputs. module dot name dot output elsewhere. Meta-arguments on a module block: count, for each, depends on, providers, version, source.

1.text: Using a module in configuration. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Providers and modules
1.text: Providers and modules. Inheritance. A child module uses the provider configurations of its parent by default. Explicit passing. The providers argument passes a configuration (for example an aliased provider) to a child. Do not put provider blocks in reusable modules. Let the caller configure providers; a module declares required providers only.

1.title: Providers and modules, continued
1.text: Providers and modules. The example is on the screen; read it line by line when you study.

1.title: Module composition and structure
1.text: Module composition and structure. Standard structure. main dot tf, variables dot tf, outputs dot tf, and a R E A D M E dot md. Small, focused modules. One purpose each (network, database, compute). Compose, do not nest deeply. The root module combines modules; pass outputs of one as inputs to another. Sensible inputs. Few, well-typed variables with defaults and descriptions. Exam tip: Compose modules in the root and connect them with outputs and inputs. Avoid hard-coded provider blocks inside a reusable module. Exam tip: Nothing crosses a module boundary except inputs and outputs. If a value is not an output, the parent cannot see it.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. How does a parent module read a value from a child module? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Through an output value of the child. Only outputs cross the module boundary toward the parent.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. How is the output vpc id of a module called network referenced? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: module.network.vpc id. Module outputs are referenced as module.N A M E.O U T P U T.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. How does a parent give a value to a module? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: By setting an argument that matches an input variable. Arguments in the module block become the values of the module's input variables.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A required input variable of a module has no value in the module block and no default. What happens on plan? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Terraform reports an error or asks for the value. A required variable must be set, so Terraform reports it or asks for it.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. A reusable module must create resources in a second region chosen by the caller. What should the caller use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: The providers argument to pass an aliased provider. The providers argument passes a provider configuration, such as an alias, to the child module.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. After adding a new module block, which command must be run before plan? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: terraform init. terraform init downloads the new module.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How does data enter a module? Answer: Through input variables. Question two. How does data leave a module? Answer: Through outputs. Question three. How is a module output referenced? Answer: module.N A M E.O U T P U T.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. Which argument passes an aliased provider? Answer: providers. Question five. What files form the standard module structure? Answer: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf and a R E A D M E. Question six. Can a parent read a child's local value? Answer: No.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Scope: module is isolated; inputs in, outputs out. Use: module block, source, inputs, init, module.N A M E.O U T P U T. Meta-arguments: count, for each, depends on, providers, version. Providers: inherited by default; providers argument to pass aliases; no provider blocks in reusable modules. Structure: main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, R E A D M E; small, composed modules.
